rattle.title: Crepitaculum infantis
rattle.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Crepitaculum infantis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: Fistula lusoria
whistle_toy.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Fistula lusoria» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Animalculum tractile
pull_toy.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Animalculum tractile» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: Arcus lusorius
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Arcus lusorius» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: Calculi sollertiae
jacks_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Calculi sollertiae» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Sortes narrativae
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Sortes narrativae» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Lusus umbrarum
shadow_play.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Lusus umbrarum» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Draco volatilis localis
kite_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Draco volatilis localis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Pupa textilis
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Pupa textilis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Pila consuta
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Pila consuta» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: Turbo localis
top_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Turbo localis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Figurae fili
string_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Figurae fili» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Tabula cursus popularis
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Tabula cursus popularis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Satio localis
sowing_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Satio localis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: Funis saltatorius
jump_rope.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Funis saltatorius» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: Lusus oculis velatis
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Lusus oculis velatis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Lucta popularis
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Lucta popularis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: Carmen memoriae
memory_song.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Carmen memoriae» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Grallae
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Grallae» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: Naviculae foliorum
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Naviculae foliorum» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: Figurae arenae/nivis
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Figurae arenae/nivis» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Pedifollis mensae
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Pedifollis mensae» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: Aenigmata localia
riddle_local.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Aenigmata localia» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Crepitaculum festivum
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Crepitaculum festivum» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: Aenigma nodorum
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Aenigma nodorum» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: Domusculus
mini_house.descTemplate: Ludicrum «Domusculus» in {country} apud {civ} notum est. Forma culturalis traditionem localem ostendit; materiae et ritus differunt. Infantes per ludum artes sociales corporeasque discunt.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

game-0001.description: Ludus notus «Chess» e regione India (Gupta / early medieval India) aetate c. 600 CE commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Orient the board so each player has a light square on the right-hand corner.
Place pieces on the back rank (rook, knight, bishop, queen on her color, king, bishop, knight, rook) with pawns on the second rank.
White moves first; players alternate moving one piece (except when castling).
Capture by landing on an opponent's piece. Win by checkmating the king.
Use special moves when legal: castling, en passant, and pawn promotion.
game-0001.name: Scaci

howToPlay: Arrange pieces on starting points on opposite sides of the river.
Red moves first; pieces move on points according to their type.
Cannons slide like chariots but capture only by jumping over exactly one screen.
Generals stay in the palace; opposing generals may not face on an open file.
Checkmate or stalemate the opposing general to win.
game-0003.name: Xiangqi

game-0004.description: Ludus notus «Shogi» e regione Japan (Heian–Muromachi Japan) aetate c. 10th–16th century commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Set pieces with pointed ends facing the opponent.
Sente moves first—move or drop one piece per turn.
Captured pieces go to your stand and may be dropped later on empty squares (with pawn/check restrictions).
Promote eligible pieces in the last three ranks.
Checkmate the opposing king to win.
game-0004.name: Shogi

Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Set checkers in the standard opening formation on the 24 points.
Roll two dice and move checkers forward using both numbers.
Hit a lone opposing blot to the bar; it must re-enter before other moves.
Stack your own checkers for safety; six consecutive points form a prime.
When all fifteen are home, bear off; first to bear off all wins.
game-0006.name: Backgammon

game-0018.description: Ludus notus «Ganjifa» e regione India (Mughal / Indian) aetate c. 16th century commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Use an 8-suit Mughal ganjifa set (96 circular cards) or a 10-suit Dashavatara set; shuffle gently without bending paint layers.
For a four-player Mughal session, deal twelve cards each; decide trump by the first suit led or a declared trump suit before play.
Players must follow the led suit if able; otherwise they may play trump or discard.
Highest trump wins the trick if any trump is played; otherwise the highest card of the led suit wins.
Each won trick scores one point (or count face cards if using a court-heavy house tally); highest trick total after all cards are played wins. Store cards flat.
game-0018.name: Ganjifa

game-0019.description: Ludus notus «Knucklebones» e regione Greece (Mediterranean antiquity) aetate c. 500 BCE or earlier commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Start with five astragali (or five jacks plus a small bounce ball if using modern replicas).
Scatter the pieces, toss one aloft (or bounce the ball once), and pick up one piece before catching the tossed piece or ball.
On later turns in the same round, pick up two, then three, then four pieces in one sweep while the toss or bounce is airborne.
Failing to catch or disturbing the remaining pile ends your turn; the next player restarts at picking up ones.
First player to complete the ones–twos–threes–fours sequence scores one point; play to five points. Use plastic or wooden replicas when real bones are unavailable.
game-0019.name: Knucklebones

howToPlay: Pick one seeker and a home base (tree, wall, or stoop); set hard bounds—no street, no locked rooms.
The seeker faces the base and counts aloud to 50 while others hide inside the bounds.
The seeker shouts “Ready or not, here I come,” then tags hiders by touch; tagged players walk to a jail spot beside home base.
A free hider may dash to base, touch it, and call “Free [name]!” to release one jailed player; if the seeker tags them on the way, they go to jail.
When all hiders are jailed, or after five minutes, the first player tagged becomes the next seeker.

howToPlay: Play Copenhagen Hnefatafl on an 11×11 board: place the king on the center throne with 12 defenders in a cross; place 24 attackers in the four edge camps.
Attackers move first. Every piece slides any number of empty squares like a rook; none may jump.
Capture an enemy by sandwiching it between two of your pieces on a rank or file (custodial capture); the throne and corner squares can help bracket.
Attackers win by capturing the king on two opposite sides (or against the throne/edge as a second side). Defenders win if the king reaches any of the four corner sanctuary squares.
Pieces may not stop on the throne except the king; attackers may not occupy the corners.

game-0061.description: Ludus notus «Dakon» e regione Indonesia (Javanese) aetate centuries old commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Use a boat board with seven small cups per side plus one large store (lumbung) at each end; place seven seeds in every small cup.
On your turn, scoop one of your cups and sow one seed clockwise into each following cup, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your store, sow again immediately from any of your cups that still hold seeds (relay turn).
If the last seed lands in an empty cup on your side, capture that seed and all seeds in the opposite cup into your store.
When one player cannot move, remaining seeds go to the owner of those cups; most seeds in store wins.
game-0061.name: Dakon

game-0062.description: Ludus notus «Sungka» e regione Philippines (Filipino) aetate centuries old commemoratur. Regulae et materiae culturales traditionem ludi servant; variationes regionales ut cognatae, non inventiones separatae, catalogantur.
howToPlay: Seat two players at a sungka board with seven small cups (bahay) per side and one head store (ulo) each; place seven cowries or seeds in every bahay.
Scoop all seeds from one of your bahay and sow counterclockwise one-by-one into each following cup, including your ulo but skipping the opponent’s ulo.
If the last seed lands in your ulo, take another turn; if it lands in an empty bahay on your side, capture the opposite bahay’s seeds into your ulo.
A player who empties their side early waits while the opponent may still sow; continue until neither side has seeds left in bahay.
Count cowries in each ulo; the higher store wins.
game-0062.name: Sungka

rattle.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κρόταλον βρέφους» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: Σῦριγξ παιγνιώδης
whistle_toy.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σῦριγξ παιγνιώδης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Ζῷον ἑλκυστόν
pull_toy.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ζῷον ἑλκυστόν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: Τόξον παιγνιώδες
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Τόξον παιγνιώδες» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: Ψῆφοι δεξιότητος
jacks_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ψῆφοι δεξιότητος» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Κλῆροι διηγηματικοί
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κλῆροι διηγηματικοί» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Παιδιὰ σκιῶν
shadow_play.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Παιδιὰ σκιῶν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Ἰκτῖνος τοπικός
kite_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ἰκτῖνος τοπικός» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Κόρη ὑφασμάτινη
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κόρη ὑφασμάτινη» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Σφαῖρα ῥαπτή
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σφαῖρα ῥαπτή» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: Στρόβιλος τοπικός
top_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Στρόβιλος τοπικός» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Σχήματα μίτου
string_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σχήματα μίτου» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Πίναξ δρόμου δημώδης
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πίναξ δρόμου δημώδης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Σπορὰ τοπική
sowing_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σπορὰ τοπική» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: Σχοινίον πηδητικόν
jump_rope.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σχοινίον πηδητικόν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: Παιδιὰ τετυφλωμένα
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Παιδιὰ τετυφλωμένα» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Πάλη δημώδης
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πάλη δημώδης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: ᾨδὴ μνήμης
memory_song.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «ᾨδὴ μνήμης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Κάλτιοι
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κάλτιοι» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: Πλοιάρια φύλλων
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πλοιάρια φύλλων» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: Μορφαὶ ἄμμου/χιόνος
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Μορφαὶ ἄμμου/χιόνος» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Ποδόσφαιρον τραπέζης
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ποδόσφαιρον τραπέζης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: Αἰνίγματα τοπικά
riddle_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Αἰνίγματα τοπικά» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Κρόταλον ἑορταστικόν
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κρόταλον ἑορταστικόν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: Αἴνιγμα κόμβων
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Αἴνιγμα κόμβων» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: Οἰκίσκος
mini_house.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Οἰκίσκος» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

howToPlay: Βῆμα 1: ἐκτέλει κατὰ τοὺς παραδοσιακοὺς κανόνας τοῦ «Xiangqi».
Βῆμα 2: ἐκτέλει κατὰ τοὺς παραδοσιακοὺς κανόνας τοῦ «Xiangqi».

game-0004.description: Τὸ παίγνιον «Shogi» ἐκ τῆς χώρας Japan (Heian–Muromachi Japan, c. 10th–16th century) μαρτυρεῖται. Οἱ κανόνες καὶ αἱ ὗλαι φυλάττουσι τὴν παράδοσιν· αἱ τοπικαὶ διαφοραὶ ὡς συγγενεῖς καταγράφονται.
howToPlay: Βῆμα 1: ἐκτέλει κατὰ τοὺς παραδοσιακοὺς κανόνας τοῦ «Shogi».
Βῆμα 2: ἐκτέλει κατὰ τοὺς παραδοσιακοὺς κανόνας τοῦ «Shogi».
Βῆμα 3: ἐκτέλει κατὰ τοὺς παραδοσιακοὺς κανόνας τοῦ «Shogi».

rattle.title: शिशुघण्टिका
rattle.descTemplate: «शिशुघण्टिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: मृत्तिकाकाष्ठसीत्कारकम्
whistle_toy.descTemplate: «मृत्तिकाकाष्ठसीत्कारकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: आकृष्यमाणपशुक्रीडनकम्
pull_toy.descTemplate: «आकृष्यमाणपशुक्रीडनकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: क्रीडनधनुः
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: «क्रीडनधनुः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: कौशलपाषाणाः
jacks_local.descTemplate: «कौशलपाषाणाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: कथाभाग्याः
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: «कथाभाग्याः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: छायाक्रीडा
shadow_play.descTemplate: «छायाक्रीडा» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: स्थानीयपतङ्गः
kite_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयपतङ्गः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: वस्त्रपुत्तलिका
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: «वस्त्रपुत्तलिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: सीव्यमानकन्दुकः
ball_sewn.descTemplate: «सीव्यमानकन्दुकः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: स्थानीयभ्रमरः
top_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयभ्रमरः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: स्थानीयसूत्ररूपाणि
string_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयसूत्ररूपाणि» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: लोकधावनफलकम्
board_race_folk.descTemplate: «लोकधावनफलकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: स्थानीयवपनम्
sowing_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयवपनम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: रज्जुप्लवनम्
jump_rope.descTemplate: «रज्जुप्लवनम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: अन्धपटक्रीडा
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: «अन्धपटक्रीडा» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: लोकमल्लयुद्धम्
wrestling_play.descTemplate: «लोकमल्लयुद्धम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: स्मृतिगीतम्
memory_song.descTemplate: «स्मृतिगीतम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: पादकाष्ठानि
balance_stilts.descTemplate: «पादकाष्ठानि» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: पर्णनौकाः
leaf_boat.descTemplate: «पर्णनौकाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: सिकताहिममूर्तयः
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: «सिकताहिममूर्तयः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: फलकपादकन्दुकः
knuckle_football.descTemplate: «फलकपादकन्दुकः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: स्थानीयप्रहेलिकाः
riddle_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयप्रहेलिकाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: उत्सवनादकम्
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: «उत्सवनादकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: ग्रन्थिप्रहेलिका
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: «ग्रन्थिप्रहेलिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: लघुगृहक्रीडनकम्
mini_house.descTemplate: «लघुगृहक्रीडनकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

game-0001.description: «Chess» इति क्रीडा India देशे (Gupta / early medieval India, c. 600 CE) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Orient the board so each player has a light square on the right-hand corner.
Place pieces on the back rank (rook, knight, bishop, queen on her color, king, bishop, knight, rook) with pawns on the second rank.
White moves first; players alternate moving one piece (except when castling).
Capture by landing on an opponent's piece. Win by checkmating the king.
Use special moves when legal: castling, en passant, and pawn promotion.
game-0001.name: शतरंजः

game-0002.description: «Go (Weiqi)» इति क्रीडा China देशे (Ancient China, c. 500 BCE or earlier) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Black places the first stone on a grid intersection.
Players alternate placing one stone; stones do not move after placement.
A group without liberties (empty adjacent intersections) is captured and removed.
Do not recreate the previous full-board position (ko) or play suicidal moves unless they capture.
When both pass, score territory plus captives (rules vary by country); higher score wins.
game-0002.name: Go (Weiqi)

game-0003.description: «Xiangqi» इति क्रीडा China देशे (Tang–Song China, c. 700–900 CE) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Arrange pieces on starting points on opposite sides of the river.
Red moves first; pieces move on points according to their type.
Cannons slide like chariots but capture only by jumping over exactly one screen.
Generals stay in the palace; opposing generals may not face on an open file.
Checkmate or stalemate the opposing general to win.
game-0003.name: Xiangqi

game-0004.description: «Shogi» इति क्रीडा Japan देशे (Heian–Muromachi Japan, c. 10th–16th century) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Set pieces with pointed ends facing the opponent.
Sente moves first—move or drop one piece per turn.
Captured pieces go to your stand and may be dropped later on empty squares (with pawn/check restrictions).
Promote eligible pieces in the last three ranks.
Checkmate the opposing king to win.
game-0004.name: Shogi

game-0005.description: «Mancala sowing games» इति क्रीडा Africa / Middle East देशे (Ancient Africa & Near East, c. 700 BCE or earlier) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Default to a Kalah-style 2×6 board: place four seeds in each of the twelve small pits; leave both end stores empty.
On your turn, scoop all seeds from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; if it lands in an empty pit on your side, capture that seed plus any seeds in the opposite pit into your store.
When one player’s six pits are empty, the opponent moves all remaining seeds into their store and the game ends.
Count seeds in each store; the higher total wins (ties are draws).
game-0005.name: Mancala sowing games

game-0006.description: «Backgammon» इति क्रीडा Persia / Mesopotamia region देशे (Ancient Near East / Persia, c. 2000 BCE ancestors; modern form later) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Set checkers in the standard opening formation on the 24 points.
Roll two dice and move checkers forward using both numbers.
Hit a lone opposing blot to the bar; it must re-enter before other moves.
Stack your own checkers for safety; six consecutive points form a prime.
When all fifteen are home, bear off; first to bear off all wins.
game-0006.name: Backgammon

game-0007.description: «Senet» इति क्रीडा Egypt देशे (Ancient Egypt, c. 3100 BCE) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: पदं 1: «Senet» क्रीडायाः पारम्परिकनियमान् अनुसर।
पदं 2: «Senet» क्रीडायाः पारम्परिकनियमान् अनुसर।
पदं 3: «Senet» क्रीडायाः पारम्परिकनियमान् अनुसर।

howToPlay: Use an 8-suit Mughal ganjifa set (96 circular cards) or a 10-suit Dashavatara set; shuffle gently without bending paint layers.
For a four-player Mughal session, deal twelve cards each; decide trump by the first suit led or a declared trump suit before play.
Players must follow the led suit if able; otherwise they may play trump or discard.
Highest trump wins the trick if any trump is played; otherwise the highest card of the led suit wins.
Each won trick scores one point (or count face cards if using a court-heavy house tally); highest trick total after all cards are played wins. Store cards flat.
game-0018.name: Ganjifa

game-0019.description: «Knucklebones» इति क्रीडा Greece देशे (Mediterranean antiquity, c. 500 BCE or earlier) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Start with five astragali (or five jacks plus a small bounce ball if using modern replicas).
Scatter the pieces, toss one aloft (or bounce the ball once), and pick up one piece before catching the tossed piece or ball.
On later turns in the same round, pick up two, then three, then four pieces in one sweep while the toss or bounce is airborne.
Failing to catch or disturbing the remaining pile ends your turn; the next player restarts at picking up ones.
First player to complete the ones–twos–threes–fours sequence scores one point; play to five points. Use plastic or wooden replicas when real bones are unavailable.
game-0019.name: Knucklebones

howToPlay: Assemble the kite; check spars and bridle balance.
With back to the wind, have a helper hold or launch as you reel tension.
Steer with line angle; climb in steady wind.
In fighter variants, maneuver to cut an opponent’s line.
Reel in before storms; never fly near power lines.

game-0022.description: «Cat's cradle» इति क्रीडा Multiple (global) देशे (Worldwide folk, unknown antiquity) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Loop a 1–2 meter cord; Player A opens Cat’s Cradle: palms facing, strings across both hands with the palmar string crossed once.
Player B pinches the two crossed X’s, pulls them out and down, then up through the center, taking the figure onto their own hands as Soldier’s Bed (or Mattress).
Player A next takes the side strings to form Candles, then Player B takes again to form the Manger (or Cradle reverse).
If any loop slips off a finger and the figure collapses, both players restart from Player A’s opening cradle.
After one clean four-step pass (Cradle → Bed → Candles → Manger), try the sequence again or learn a solo figure such as Cup and Saucer.
game-0022.name: Cat's cradle

game-0023.description: «Jianzi (shuttlecock kicking)» इति क्रीडा China देशे (Chinese folk, Han legends; popular later dynasties) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Toss the shuttlecock onto your foot.
Kick with inner foot, outer foot, or knee to keep it airborne.
Count consecutive kicks; restart on a drop.
In a circle, pass to neighbors without using hands.
Agree whether hand saves are allowed (usually not).
game-0023.name: Jianzi (shuttlecock kicking)

game-0024.description: «Sepak takraw» इति क्रीडा Thailand / Malaysia देशे (Southeast Asian, centuries old; modern sport 20th c.) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Mark a court about 13.4 × 6.1 m with a net 1.52 m high (men’s sport height) and use a rattan or synthetic takraw ball.
Each team of three stands on its side; the server’s teammate tosses the ball for a foot serve over the net into the opponent’s court.
A side may use at most three touches with foot, knee, chest, or head before sending the ball back; hands and arms are faults.
Score one point when the ball grounds in the opponent’s court or the opponent faults (net touch with hand, four touches, out of bounds).
Play to 21 points per set (must win by 2); best of three sets decides the match.
game-0024.name: Sepak takraw

Teams grip evenly; avoid wrapping the rope around limbs in sport rules.
On a signal, pull with short coordinated heaves.
Win by pulling the center marker across your line.
Stop immediately if someone slips dangerously.
game-0037.name: Tug of war

game-0038.description: «Hide-and-seek» इति क्रीडा Multiple (global) देशे (Worldwide childhood, unknown antiquity) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Pick one seeker and a home base (tree, wall, or stoop); set hard bounds—no street, no locked rooms.
The seeker faces the base and counts aloud to 50 while others hide inside the bounds.
The seeker shouts “Ready or not, here I come,” then tags hiders by touch; tagged players walk to a jail spot beside home base.
A free hider may dash to base, touch it, and call “Free [name]!” to release one jailed player; if the seeker tags them on the way, they go to jail.
When all hiders are jailed, or after five minutes, the first player tagged becomes the next seeker.
game-0038.name: Hide-and-seek

game-0039.description: «Hopscotch» इति क्रीडा Multiple (global; Roman roots often cited) देशे (Worldwide childhood, ancient–present) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Draw a numbered hopscotch grid.
Toss a marker into the next square; it must land cleanly inside.
Hop through on one foot, skipping the occupied square.
Retrieve the marker on the return without faults.
First to complete all numbers wins.
game-0039.name: Hopscotch

howToPlay: Draw a circle and place target marbles inside.
Knuckle-shoot from the edge to knock targets out.
Captured marbles score or are kept depending on agreed stakes.
If your shooter remains in-ring, many rules allow another shot from there.
Clear the ring or reach a point goal to win.
game-0040.name: Marbles

howToPlay: Wind string around the body or prepare a whip.
Launch with a smooth pull so the tip spins on hard ground.
Optionally whip to add energy.
Compete for longest spin or for knocking out rivals.
Repair worn tips as needed.
game-0041.name: Spinning top

game-0042.description: «Hnefatafl» इति क्रीडा Norway देशे (Norse, c. 400–1000 CE) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Play Copenhagen Hnefatafl on an 11×11 board: place the king on the center throne with 12 defenders in a cross; place 24 attackers in the four edge camps.
Attackers move first. Every piece slides any number of empty squares like a rook; none may jump.
Capture an enemy by sandwiching it between two of your pieces on a rank or file (custodial capture); the throne and corner squares can help bracket.
Attackers win by capturing the king on two opposite sides (or against the throne/edge as a second side). Defenders win if the king reaches any of the four corner sanctuary squares.
Pieces may not stop on the throne except the king; attackers may not occupy the corners.
game-0042.name: Hnefatafl

game-0043.description: «Fox and Geese» इति क्रीडा United Kingdom देशे (Northern European folk, medieval) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Place geese on one end and the fox centrally or opposite per rules.
Geese move first or second by agreement; they walk without jumping.
Fox may jump adjacent geese to capture.
Geese win by immobilizing the fox; fox wins by capturing enough geese.
Use a modern printed fox-and-geese board if historic boards are unavailable.

game-0061.description: «Dakon» इति क्रीडा Indonesia देशे (Javanese, centuries old) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Use a boat board with seven small cups per side plus one large store (lumbung) at each end; place seven seeds in every small cup.
On your turn, scoop one of your cups and sow one seed clockwise into each following cup, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your store, sow again immediately from any of your cups that still hold seeds (relay turn).
If the last seed lands in an empty cup on your side, capture that seed and all seeds in the opposite cup into your store.
When one player cannot move, remaining seeds go to the owner of those cups; most seeds in store wins.
game-0061.name: Dakon

game-0062.description: «Sungka» इति क्रीडा Philippines देशे (Filipino, centuries old) प्रसिद्धा। नियमाः द्रव्याणि च परम्परां रक्षन्ति; देशभेदाः सजातित्वेन गण्यन्ते।
howToPlay: Seat two players at a sungka board with seven small cups (bahay) per side and one head store (ulo) each; place seven cowries or seeds in every bahay.
Scoop all seeds from one of your bahay and sow counterclockwise one-by-one into each following cup, including your ulo but skipping the opponent’s ulo.
If the last seed lands in your ulo, take another turn; if it lands in an empty bahay on your side, capture the opposite bahay’s seeds into your ulo.
A player who empties their side early waits while the opponent may still sow; continue until neither side has seeds left in bahay.
Count cowries in each ulo; the higher store wins.
game-0062.name: Sungka
